outline.chapter_title: Introduction to Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
outline.description: This chapter introduces the challenges of mathematical reasoning for LLMs and sets the stage for the DeepSeekMath project, contrasting the current landscape of open-source and proprietary models.
subtopics: The complexity of mathematical reasoning vs. general language tasks
Evaluation benchmarks: GSM8K, MATH, and competition-level reasoning
The gap between open-source models and proprietary models (GPT-4, Gemini-Ultra)
Overview of the DeepSeekMath architecture and training stages

outline.description: This chapter details the creation of the DeepSeekMath Corpus and the impact of specialized pre-training data on a model's reasoning capabilities.
subtopics: The DeepSeekMath Corpus: Sourcing 120B tokens from Common Crawl
Iterative Data Selection Pipeline: Using fastText classifiers and human annotation
Data Decontamination: Preventing benchmark leakage
The role of code training: Why initializing with DeepSeek-Coder helps mathematical reasoning
Analysis of data sources: The surprising ineffectiveness of arXiv papers
Multilingual mathematical data and its impact on cross-lingual reasoning

outline.description: This chapter explains the transition from a base model to an instruction-tuned model, focusing on the different formats of mathematical solution generation.
subtopics: Mathematical Instruction Tuning: Goals and Data Curation
Reasoning Formats: Chain-of-Thought (CoT), Program-of-Thought (PoT), and Tool-Integrated Reasoning
Building the SFT dataset: Integrating English and Chinese K-12 and competition problems
Evaluating DeepSeekMath-Instruct: Performance metrics without vs. with tool use

outline.chapter_title: Reinforcement Learning: From PPO to GRPO
outline.description: This chapter provides a deep dive into the Reinforcement Learning (RL) phase, introducing the Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) algorithm as an efficient alternative to PPO.
subtopics: Basics of Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO): Actor-Critic architecture and the value function
The memory and computational bottleneck of the Critic model
Introduction to Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)
Mechanism of GRPO: Baseline estimation via group scores
Calculating advantages using relative rewards
KL Divergence regularization in GRPO

outline.description: This chapter explores different supervision methods and iterative training processes used to further refine the model's mathematical accuracy.
subtopics: Outcome Supervision: Rewards based on final answer correctness
Process Supervision: Step-by-step reward modeling for complex reasoning
Iterative RL: Updating the reward model and policy in a feedback loop
Replay mechanisms for stable reward model training
Comparing outcome-based vs. process-based RL performance

outline.chapter_title: A Unified Paradigm for Alignment and RL
outline.description: This chapter synthesizes various training methods into a single framework to analyze how data sources, reward functions, and algorithms contribute to model improvement.
subtopics: The Unified Gradient Equation: Data Source, Reward Function, and Algorithm
Comparing SFT, RFT, DPO, PPO, and GRPO within the paradigm
Online vs. Offline Sampling: The superiority of real-time exploration
Gradient Coefficients: How GRPO handles positive and negative reinforcement differently than RFT
The 'Misalignment' problem: Understanding Maj@K vs. Pass@K performance

outline.description: The final chapter discusses why RL is effective, the current limitations of the DeepSeekMath model, and the roadmap for future research in mathematical LLMs.
subtopics: Does RL improve fundamental capability or output distribution? (Robustness vs. Capability)
Current limitations: Geometry, theorem proving, and few-shot capabilities
Future Directions: Advanced decoding (Tree-search), Weak-to-Strong alignment
Improving Reward Model generalization and uncertainty estimation
Conclusion: The path toward open-source mathematical parity with proprietary models
